about: The volume table for the Load estimate. Cubic feet per item from the Washington UTC sample cube sheet and two movers' household goods survey reports; pounds from the EPA volume-to-weight factors. Where sources differ, the larger volume is used, so an estimate errs toward more of the truck (judgment call). Items marked judgment are our own figures: check them by eye.

truck.size: 10 ft long, 8 ft wide, 5 ft high
truck.basis: 1-800-GOT-JUNK? sizes its full truck at 10 ft long, 5 ft high and 8 ft wide (400 cubic feet), charges by eighths of it, and says its trucks hold roughly two tons. Fixr's full load is 350 to 475 cubic feet; HomeAdvisor's 13 to 17 cubic yards.

pickup.basis: LawnStarter: a pickup truck holds about 3.5 cubic yards. A "pickup load" or "truckload" typed in a list counts this much.

weight.basis: Items without their own EPA weight count 7 pounds a cubic foot, the movers' constructive weight in Washington's household goods tariff. Junk is often lighter, so the weight and the dump fee err high: weigh a few of your own loads.

unknown.basis: Anything not in the table counts 10 cubic feet (judgment call) and is listed for you to check by eye.

material_without_amount.basis: A material typed without an amount ("drywall") counts 10 cubic feet (judgment call) and is listed: type it like "1 cubic yard of drywall" or "2 pickup loads of brush".

heavy_share.basis: When construction debris, dirt, concrete, rock or shingles make up half the volume or more, the load is priced as heavy debris (judgment call).

eighths.basis: 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full truck are priced from your menu; 3/8, 5/8 and 7/8 are halfway between their neighbors, rounded the way the menu rounds (judgment call).

wa_tariff.publisher: Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission, Tariff 15-C (household goods)

gj.says: Full truckload 10 ft long x 5 ft high x 8 ft wide; half truckload 5 x 5 x 8; minimum to 1/4 load 50 to 100 cubic feet, 1/4 to 1/2 load 100 to 200, 1/2 to full load 200 to 400. Charges in 1/8 increments of the truck by how much space the items take up. Trucks hold roughly two tons of junk, the same as eight standard sized refrigerators or six full-sized three-seater sofas. Prices include disposal and environmental fees.

fx.says: Price by load (labor included): 1/8 load 60 to 80 cubic feet $75 to $125; 1/4 load 80 to 120 cubic feet $125 to $175; half load 120 to 300 cubic feet $175 to $375; 3/4 load 300 to 350 cubic feet $375 to $450; full load 350 to 475 cubic feet $450 to $650; $1.25 to $2.08 per cubic foot.

ha.says: Truck load, volume, average cost: 1/8 2 to 3 cubic yards $75 to $125; 1/4 3 to 4.5 cubic yards $125 to $200; 1/2 4.5 to 11 cubic yards $200 to $400; 3/4 11 to 13 cubic yards $400 to $600; full 13 to 17 cubic yards $600 to $800.

ls.says: Pickup truck: about 3.5 cubic yards; dump truck up to 20 cubic yards; 1 cubic yard is a 3 ft x 3 ft x 3 ft box (27 cubic feet); full truck up to 20 cubic yards, average $675.

fx_items.says: Item removal: pool table $400 to $600; piano $200 to $400; hot tub $150 to $600; refrigerator $100 to $200; freezer $100 to $200; couch $100 to $200; mattress $75 to $150; tires $60 to $90.
